title: Actual internal derived tensor arrow on resolving representatives
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-étale site, small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the pulled-back ring object $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and the fixed exact internal/section module equivalence $E_T$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary operations and universe convention of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Let $q_T^{\mathrm i},q_T^{\mathrm s}$ denote the internal and section homotopy-to-derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm i},\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm s}$ for the full subcategories of K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with the corresponding exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests internally. All total tensors below are signed direct-sum cochain totals [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and all derived tensors are relative to $R_T$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $F=f^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and $LF$ the specified total derived section pullback with comparison $\epsilon_A:LF(q_Y^{\mathrm s}A)\to q_X^{\mathrm s}(FA)$ of [def-pd-section-derived-realization]. Use the derived pullback comparison $\gamma:D(E_X)Lf^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong LF D(E_Y)$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization], compatible with these resolution transformations, and the normalized $\theta_T,e_T$ of [lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison]. Let $\delta_f$ be the actual internal derived oplax tensor transformation obtained by localizing the actual internal total arrow of [def-pd-proetale-section-module-functors], using the internal tensor localization [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] and derived module pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\widehat\delta_f$ for this transformation conjugated by $D(E_X),D(E_Y),\gamma,\theta_X,\theta_Y$ to a transformation
$$ LF(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\longrightarrow LF(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}LF(N)$$
on section-derived objects. For every $P,Q\in\mathcal P_Y^{\mathrm s}$ let $r_Y:q_Y^{\mathrm s}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong q_Y^{\mathrm s}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}q_Y^{\mathrm s}Q$ and $r_X:q_X^{\mathrm s}\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FQ)\cong q_X^{\mathrm s}FP\otimes^{\mathbf L}q_X^{\mathrm s}FQ$ be the fixed ringed representative comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $b_{P,Q}$ be the fixed totalized ordinary comparison [lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison], and put
$$a_{P,Q}=\epsilon_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}\circ LF(r_Y^{-1}),\qquad c_{P,Q}=r_X^{-1}\circ(\epsilon_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_Q).$$
These are invertible and the actual internal map satisfies the specified representative equation
$$c_{P,Q}\circ\widehat\delta_{f;q_Y^{\mathrm s}P,q_Y^{\mathrm s}Q}=q_X^{\mathrm s}(b_{P,Q})\circ a_{P,Q}.$$
Its source is $LF(q_Y^{\mathrm s}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}q_Y^{\mathrm s}Q)$ and its target is $q_X^{\mathrm s}\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FQ)$. The equation is natural on representatives and compatible with inversion of their quasi-isomorphisms; it compares the actual internal map, not a map defined anew by the right side. If $\widehat u_f:LF(R_Y[0])\to R_X[0]$ is the actual internal derived unit conjugated by $\gamma,e_Y,e_X$, and $u_f:F(R_Y[0])\cong R_X[0]$ is the ordinary scalar unit, then $\widehat u_f=q_X^{\mathrm s}(u_f)\circ\epsilon_{R_Y[0]}$. On resolving triples and on pairs with the regular degree-zero unit, the actual internal associator and unitor diagrams become the localized cochain diagrams of [lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison] through exactly these resolution comparisons. No equality with the independently specified ringed derived tensor-pullback transformation is assumed.

proof.text: The section pullback is exact, so each specified epsilon is the component of mapDerivedCategoryFactors and is invertible on every complex. The TensorRepresentativeCondition supplied by [lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison] makes qTensor invertible on a resolving pair, hence input is invertible. The actual internalDelta is a natural isomorphism, and its conjugate is therefore invertible. After establishing the representative equation in Step 2, output is invertible by cancellation against that actual conjugate, since the ordinary total comparison is an isomorphism. No separate pullback preservation or computation theorem is required for these invertibility assertions.

proof.text: Use the proved source-library formula Functor.leftDerivedTensorComparison_app_app_comp_tensorHom on the homotopy images of the internal preimages supplied by [lem-pd-section-resolution-conjugation-identities]. This formula holds for arbitrary complexes. The quotient-to-derived lax tensor map simplifies to the homotopy-to-derived lax tensor map, since the quotient factor isomorphisms and tensor maps are identities. Use the proved forward-projection API of [def-pd-section-total-oplax-comparison-data] to normalize the specified internal total arrow using its fixed ordinary monoidal structure and apply D(E_X) to this equation. For arbitrary section resolving P,Q, the explicit SubstitutionEquations for the termwise counits identify the input, output and middle arrow. A generic two-stage naturality calculation extends the actual conjugate through the localization comparisons and equivalence counits. Combine these substitution identities with the mapped internal component equation by associativity, and cancel the invertible binary input identification. The result is exactly actualPath = cochainPath with the prescribed input and output maps.

proof.text: The internal component lemma gives $v^{\mathrm i}=q^{\mathrm i}(u^{\mathrm i})\eta$. Substitute this in the unary identity of [lem-pd-section-resolution-conjugation-identities] and cancel $LF(e_Y)\gamma$ on the right. Its left side is the prescribed conjugate unit, hence $\widehat u_f=q^{\mathrm s}(u_f)\epsilon_{R_Y[0]}$.

proof.text: Whisker the natural transformation conjugating the actual internal delta by the product localization functor. Compose it with the tensor of the natural epsilon transformation and then qTensor. Naturality of this composite is precisely naturality of actualPath for arbitrary cochain maps, hence for resolving representatives. The stated inverse equations and composition alone give inverse naturality, without any further tensor computation or quasi-isomorphism premise.

proof.text: Use [lem-pd-section-resolving-oplax-constraint-diagrams] with $\mu=\widehat\delta_f$ and $v=\widehat u_f$. Steps 2–3 verify its pair and unit hypotheses with exactly the prescribed $r,\epsilon$. Its nested total closure permits resolving triples; its path identities give precisely the localized cochain associator and both unitor diagrams through those same vertex comparisons, including the conjugated internal constraints. The generic constraint formulas require only the cochain tensor data records, and are shared data definitions used by the public normalization predicates and the generic normalization proof. Whole-proposition reflexivity checks preserve the original associator and unitor predicates; the final specialization only unfolds the named model tensor and rewrites the fixed regular comparison and actual tensor components.
